fields.sections.0.h: The Aaron Swartz case: excessive legal punishment
fields.sections.1.h: Meta's large-scale data collection: minor legal liability
fields.sections.2.h: Fundamental difference in the purpose of the two cases
fields.sections.3.h: The author's personal anger and activist stance
fields.sections.0.ko: RSS protocol co-developer Aaron Swartz was prosecuted for downloading approximately 70 gigabytes of academic papers from JSTOR, an academic paper database. Authorities sought to impose extreme punishment of 35 years imprisonment, a $1 million fine, and asset seizure, and under the pressure of this excessive punishment, Swartz ultimately made an extreme choice. The author describes this as substantive 'murder' by the legal system and points to it as a moral failure of society as a whole.
fields.sections.1.ko: In contrast, Meta (formerly Facebook) collected approximately 80 terabytes of book data for AI model training, yet the legal consequences are minimal. Meta is likely to face only minor financial penalties in potential future court litigation, while continuing to generate revenue from AI models in the meantime. This stands in stark contrast to the harsh punishment Swartz faced.
fields.sections.2.ko: The author emphasizes that the disparity in legal treatment between the two should not be understood merely as a difference in scale. Swartz's action aimed at knowledge dissemination and archiving of academic materials, while Meta's collection originated from a distinctly different purpose: developing proprietary commercial AI models. The author criticizes Meta's technology as a system that "harms the environment" and damages the CEO's mental health while making the world's richest person even richer.
fields.sections.3.ko: The author expresses anger on behalf of Swartz, whom he has never met in person, and reveals deep frustration, uncertain where to direct these feelings. Acknowledging that this emotion is pushing him toward a more radical stance, the author suggests at the end of the piece, with irony, the fundamental need for change regarding technology billionaires.
fields.caveat: The author's personal anger and radicalized perspective are strongly evident, so the legal and technical details of the two cases should be independently verified through source links in the original text and official records of each case.
